seo.title: Snowflake client for {devices}
seo.description: Sign in to Snowflake with a key pair, browser SSO, OAuth or a password and passcode, switch warehouse and role without reconnecting, and unload to a stage.

header.title: Snowflake client for {devices}
header.lead: Sign in the way your account requires, move the session between warehouses and roles without reconnecting, then query, edit and unload tables to a stage.

sections.title: Connect and sign in
paragraphs: Enter the account identifier, such as myorg-myaccount or a legacy locator like xy12345.us-east-1: whatever sits in front of .snowflakecomputing.com. Every request goes over HTTPS to that account’s endpoint, so there is no host, no SSL section and no SSH pane.

Pick an <ui>Auth Method</ui> and the form shows only what it needs. A key pair signs each connect with your PKCS#8 private key, so the Mac’s clock has to be right. Browser SSO sends you to your identity provider. An OAuth token is used as pasted and never refreshed. A password goes with a current code in <ui>MFA Passcode (TOTP)</ui> when the account enforces MFA.

With ALLOW_CLIENT_MFA_CACHING on the account, one fresh passcode is enough: Snowflake returns an MFA token that TablePro keeps in the Keychain. With ALLOW_ID_TOKEN, browser SSO keeps a sign-in token there, and later connects skip the browser until Snowflake rejects it.
Snowflake has no URL scheme. Name a section in CLI Connection Name instead, and every field you leave empty is read from ~/.snowflake/connections.toml when you connect.

sections.title: Warehouses, roles and queries
paragraphs: Database > Session Context moves the session to another warehouse or role with USE WAREHOUSE and USE ROLE, without reconnecting. One TablePro connection is one Snowflake session, kept open while idle, and a tab bound to a second database runs USE DATABASE ahead of its statements on that same session.

The sidebar groups objects by database and schema. Object lists come from SHOW commands, which run without a warehouse; column details come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA, which needs one. Explain returns Snowflake’s plan as raw text.

Grid edits bind their values on the server, with VARIANT, OBJECT and ARRAY cells sent through PARSE_JSON. An edit keys on the declared primary key, or on every column when there is none. Snowflake never enforces key constraints, so a duplicated key value means an edit or a delete reaches every matching row: check a table for duplicates before you edit it.

sections.title: Structure
paragraphs: The DDL view comes from GET_DDL. The Structure tab adds, renames and drops columns, sets NOT NULL, comments and the primary key, widens a VARCHAR, and changes a NUMBER’s precision at the same scale.
Changes Snowflake would reject are refused before anything runs: shrinking a VARCHAR, any other type change, and setting a column default to a new value. Clearing a default runs.

sections.title: Move data
paragraphs: <importData>Import</importData> {importFormats} files through the connection, and export a table or a result to your Mac as {exportFormats}.

To unload a table without passing it through your Mac, choose File > Server-Side Export… and name a stage, with or without its @. Server-Side Export runs COPY INTO with your own privileges and writes gzipped CSV, Parquet or JSON; the sheet waits until the unload finishes, and nothing lands on the Mac.

faq.question: Why does the sidebar show tables but no columns?
faq.answer: Column details come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA, which needs a running warehouse. Set Warehouse on the connection or in Session Context. A database whose objects do not appear at all needs USAGE granted to the connecting role.

faq.question: Why do TIMESTAMP_LTZ values show in UTC?
faq.answer: TablePro reads them as a UTC time, marked Z, rather than converting them to the session’s TIMEZONE.

faq.question: Key pair sign-in says the JWT token is invalid. What should I check?
faq.answer: The token carries your account locator and a timestamp. Check the account identifier and the Mac’s clock, then confirm the public key is registered on the user with ALTER USER … SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY.
